correctness.rationale: The hyperbolic lattice U has D²=2xy and gcd(x,y)=1 for primitivity; Festi Proposition 3.3 gives y>x>0. Assign each prime-power block of d to one of two coprime factors, exchanging sides gives 2^{omega(d)−1}. Isotropic classes have xy=0 and nef fiber is uniquely f; (-2)-classes satisfy xy=−1, effective one is O=e−f. The K3 big-nef base-divisor criterion gives fixed section precisely D=O+(y+1)F (x=1); primitive ample classes with x>=2 are base-point free. Saint-Donat very-ampleness criterion detects degree-two intersection with elliptic F at x=2; for x>=3 no hyperelliptic obstruction or divisibility on this lattice, so very ample. Primitive minimal coprime factor pairs x>=2 (2,3), x>=3 (3,4); counting x=2 requires d=2m with odd m>1. Independently enumerated pairs d=6,12,14,30,42,60,210; source script checks 2<=d<=5000 but no finite enumeration substitutes for geometric criteria.

value.rationale: A complete arithmetic count of globally generated and projectively embedding primitive ample classes on the Picard-rank-two order-three example is a natural geometric classification. It corrects the misleading impression that the source’s uniform ample polarizations are automatically morphism-producing, and gives sharp first degree 12/24 thresholds; it is more than a random lattice enumeration.

final_claim: On the complex Picard-U K3 surface with F=f, O=e−f and ample cone y>x>0 used by Festi, primitive ample degree 2d classes (d>1) correspond exactly to coprime factors xy=d,x<y, hence count 2^{omega(d)−1}; D is base-point free iff x>=2 and very ample iff x>=3. The first such squares are 12 and 24; the uniform ample e+df has fixed O. Refined counts subtract the unique x=1 factor and, for very ampleness, x=2 iff v2(d)=1 and d>2.
limitations: K3 classification relies on the classical Mayer/Saint-Donat global-generation and very-ampleness theorems, not a new proof of them.
Restriction to complex marked Picard U surface and primitive ample classes; no embedding equations or polarized-moduli counts.
